ENGLISH — MOCK EXAM #18
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. going
   C. goes
   D. went

3. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.

4. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

5. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

7. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. quickly
   D. blue

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

11. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

12. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

13. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. No full stops

14. When practising Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.

15. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Subject-verb agreement. and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.4.1 Functional Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
